statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-6042: the GB18030 4-byte decoder in musl's iconv() (src/locale/iconv.c), in musl up to 1.2.6, finds the unmapped character for a 4-byte sequence by repeatedly scanning the whole 2-byte mapping table, so a crafted GB18030 input can take hundreds of milliseconds per character to decode and exhaust CPU (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/04/02/10). Upstream fixed it in commit https://git.musl-libc.org/cgit/musl/commit/?id=67219f0130ec7c876ac0b299046460fad31caabf, which replaces the scan with a lookup in a new 206-entry table of unmapped ranges. Alpine applies that commit as CVE-2026-6042.patch and lists the fix in musl 1.2.5-r22 for Alpine 3.23 (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json). The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes musl 1.2.5-r10, 1.2.5-r21, 1.2.5-r22, 1.2.5-r23 and 1.2.5-r24, built from Alpine's musl package source. We checked the musl package (the shared C library and dynamic loader) and the musl-dev package (the static libc.a) of every build for x86_64 and aarch64 against the index checksum: the range table the fix adds is present in both files from 1.2.5-r22 on and absent from 1.2.5-r10 and 1.2.5-r21, while the GB18030 converter itself is present in every build. The range ends at 1.2.5-r22.
